function: NN receivers for MIMO RSMA: 1D-CNN channel estimation and DNN symbol detection of common and private streams (RS-Net, RS-Net+, Joint-Net), replacing SIC blocks (p. 5, p. 6).
system: Downlink MU-MIMO 1-layer RSMA: BS NT=3 or 6 antennas, K=2 users with NR=1 or 2 (K=4 overloaded); QPSK/16QAM; no RIS; band not stated (p. 4, p. 8, p. 14).
method: Supervised: shallow 1D-CNN channel estimator and MLP symbol detectors (Adagrad, cross-entropy), trained offline for each SNR, no per-channel retraining; hybrid model/data-driven SIC (p. 6, p. 7, p. 8).
data_channel: Simulated (Sionna) Gaussian MIMO channels, separable-covariance ULA model for overloaded case; 10^4 training examples (10^5 for 16QAM), 20% validation (p. 4, p. 8, p. 11, p. 14).
test_conditions: Same-scenario training and testing (NT, NR, K, modulation, channel statistics), one NN per SNR; results cover SNR, precoder noise, CSIR source, clipping (p. 7, p. 8, p. 16).
baselines: Non-learned: ML (full CSI), LMMSE, SIC detectors with LS channel estimation. Learned: RS-Net (own earlier work [36]), RS-Net+, Joint-Net, all the paper's architectures (p. 3, p. 5, p. 9).
metrics: Symbol error rate of common and private streams, NMSE of channel estimation, number of multiplications and additions (p. 9, p. 10, p. 16).
complexity: Closed-form counts of multiplications and additions per detector (Table 2, p. 17); Fig. 23 total operations; RS-Net+ about 50x MMSE/SIC for QPSK (p. 16, p. 17).
q1_support: p. 4: "which is Gaussian distributed" for the channel matrix; the overloaded case uses a separable-covariance ULA model (p. 14). Sionna is named only as the implementation library (p. 8); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data is stated.
q2_support: p. 7: "as long as the system scenario i.e., number of transmit antennas, users, and channel statistics remains unchanged"; p. 16: "as test dataset does not deviate from training dataset"; the CSIR-input comparisons (Figs. 12, 22) vary only the CSI quality, and each scenario has its own trained networks (Table 1, p. 11).
q3_support: p. 5: "we adopt as benchmarks (i) the Maximum Likelihood (ML) detector" plus LMMSE and SIC (non-learned). Learned comparisons are only among the paper's own architectures; RS-Net is p. 3: "which leverages our previous work in [36]" and is the base of RS-Net+; no earlier learned receiver ([19]-[23]) is simulated.
q4_support: p. 16: "Table 2 summarizes the number of additions and multiplications needed" by each detector, with Fig. 23 total operations; p. 16: "50x increase in the case of RS-Net+" relative to MMSE and SIC for QPSK.
q5_support: p. 8: "The communication system has been implemented using Sionna" (a third-party open-source library); the training data are self-generated by simulation (p. 7, p. 10) and the paper gives no link to its own code or data.
notes: Area 1: channel estimation (1D-CNN) and symbol detection (MLP) work together, and the main metric is the SER (Figs. 11-13, 16, 21, 22), so detection wins over estimation (NMSE, Figs. 9, 10, 15, 20); RSMA is the transmission scheme, not area 5 or 7. The channel is described as Gaussian or separable-covariance, with no 3GPP model stated although Sionna is used. q3 judgement: RS-Net comes from the authors' earlier conference paper [36] (p. 3) and could count as an earlier learned baseline, but the paper presents it as one of its three own architectures and as RS-Net+ without the soft-information module, so q3 is 0; it would be 1 if the reviewer counts RS-Net as the earlier published baseline.
